title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
blurb: Mole gives up on spring-cleaning and meets the Water Rat. Boats, the river, and long happy sentences.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
blurb: Alice follows the White Rabbit down the hole. Playful, with bracketed asides and words that sound alike.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: Watson walks in on a client with fiery red hair. Dialogue-heavy, with some long formal sentences.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
chapter: Chapter I: The Old Sea-dog at the Admiral Benbow
blurb: An old seaman takes a room at the inn. Dense, old-fashioned prose with the longest sentences of the four.
